title: core.skeleton — bone hierarchy with a numeric canonical rest pose
description: A skeleton, its rest pose as NUMBERS (law 8: canonical poses are numbers, not words), and the retarget maps that let a foreign rig bind to it. The canonical humanoid instance of this schema is spec/skeleton/canonical-humanoid-v1.json. An optional binary mirror for very large rigs is described by spec/layouts/skeleton.layout.txt.

status.description: LIFECYCLE STATE, not a version. A skeleton is painful to change after v1, so a skeleton that has not been approved says so out loud. The version an approved skeleton carries lives in canon_version, deliberately in a separate field: a value that is both a state and a number is a field two readers disagree about.

canon_version.description: The approved version of this canon, e.g. "1.0". Present when status is "approved"; meaningless while it is "draft". Distinct from schema_version, which versions the SHAPE of this file, and from a node version, which is an incremental integer: this is the version of the NUMBERS, and it is the string a rig or a clip cites when it says which canon it was authored against.

approval.description: Who approved these numbers and under what decision, so the approval is a record rather than a state change nobody can trace. Law 6 applied to a canon: the reasoning travels with the artifact.

ruling.description: The decision record this approval rests on, named so a reader can go and read it.

extends.description: skeleton_id of a base skeleton this one adds bones to. An extension file (e.g. core.hands.v1) declares only its own bones and attaches them by naming an existing bone as parent. A consumer that does not load the extension keeps a working base skeleton (law 3).

extensions.description: skeleton_ids of known extensions to this skeleton. Advisory: the extension file is the authority on its own bones.

conventions.description: Restated inside the payload so the skeleton is an island (law 3). Every value MUST match the manifest's conventions block; a reader that finds a mismatch MUST refuse the node rather than reconcile it.

bone_axis_along.description: The bone-local axis that points from the bone's head toward its tail. Blender's convention, chosen because it is the most widely documented one.

bone_axis_back.description: The bone-local axis that points along the bone's declared dorsal reference direction. Together with bone_axis_along this fixes the roll, which is the degree of freedom that silently ruins retargeting when left undeclared.

composition.description: Column-vector convention: a point p in bone space becomes M_bone * p in model space. Translation is applied before rotation within a bone, i.e. rest_translation is expressed in the PARENT's frame.

reference_height_m.description: The stature this rest pose was authored for. A retargeter scales root translation by target_height / reference_height_m.

pose_name.description: e.g. 't-pose-palms-down'. The numbers are the definition; this is the label for humans.

floor_plane.description: Where the ground is in this skeleton's model space, so a consumer knows whether the origin is between the feet or at the hips.

bone_id.description: Unique within the skeleton including its extensions.

parent.description: bone_id of the parent, or null for a root. Bones MUST be listed with every parent before its children.

rest_rotation.description: Unit quaternion [w,x,y,z], LOCAL: the bone's rest orientation relative to its parent's frame. This is the value an animation track replaces.

rest_translation.description: Metres, expressed in the PARENT bone's frame. For a root bone, in model space.

length_m.description: Head-to-tail length. The tail is at bone-local (0, length_m, 0).

model_rest_rotation.description: Unit quaternion [w,x,y,z] of the same rest pose in MODEL space. Redundant with the local values by construction, and present on purpose: it is what makes the local numbers checkable by hand, and law 8's corollary prefers a declared value over a derived one. A reader MUST verify that composing the local chain reproduces this within 1e-5 per component, and MUST report a skeleton where it does not.

model_rest_head_m.description: Model-space position of the bone's head (its origin), metres.

model_rest_tail_m.description: Model-space position of the bone's tail, metres. Equals model_rest_head_m + length_m * axis_along.

axis_along.description: Model-space unit vector the bone's local +Y maps to in the rest pose.

axis_back.description: Model-space unit vector the bone's local +Z maps to in the rest pose. Orthogonal to axis_along.

role.description: Semantic role, so a retargeter can match by meaning rather than by name spelling.

mirror_of.description: bone_id of this bone's left/right twin, when it has one.

limits.description: Optional joint limits, as a swing-twist decomposition about the bone's own axes. Radians.

retarget.description: Name maps from foreign rigs onto this skeleton's bone_ids. A map is DATA, not code, and a reader that has never heard of the foreign rig can still apply it.

map.description: foreign bone name -> this skeleton's bone_id. A foreign bone with no entry is ignored; one of our bones with no source is left at rest.

calibration_pose.description: One pose, in this skeleton's own bone_ids, that a foreign rig is put into so a solver can compute the per-bone orientation offsets. Conformance test 3 uses it. Absent means the rest pose itself is the calibration pose.

rotations.description: bone_id -> local quaternion [w,x,y,z]. Bones not listed are at their rest rotation.

sha256.description: Hash of the WKSK file that mirrors this JSON. The mirror also carries this JSON's hash in its own header, so staleness is detectable from either side.
